description: Erth is Abu Dhabi's modern Emirati fine-dining reference, set beside Al Hosn and the Cultural Foundation. The kitchen turns local memory, regional produce and Emirati hospitality into a polished tasting-led experience that feels rooted rather than ceremonial.
highlights: One Michelin star, modern Emirati cuisine, cultural-district setting and strong local identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Time Out Abu Dhabi; FACT Dining Awards; Official website

description: Talea brings Antonio Guida's refined Italian cooking to Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental, translating cucina di famiglia into a polished luxury-hotel dining room. The experience is elegant without feeling stiff, with precise pastas, seafood and northern Italian technique matched to one of Abu Dhabi's grandest settings.
highlights: One Michelin star, contemporary Italian cooking and a grand Emirates Palace setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards; Mandarin Oriental
hotel_name_hint: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Abu Dhabi

description: Hakkasan Abu Dhabi is the capital's most established luxury Cantonese dining room, combining the brand's dark, polished glamour with the scale of Emirates Palace. It remains a serious special-occasion address for dim sum, roast meats, seafood and high-end Cantonese signatures.
highlights: One Michelin star, opulent Cantonese dining, terrace and Emirates Palace location.
sources: Michelin Guide; Condé Nast Traveler; FACT Dining Awards; Official website
hotel_name_hint: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Abu Dhabi

description: NIRI is Abu Dhabi's strongest contemporary Japanese success story, mixing yakitori, sushi-counter energy and a polished highball-bar spirit on Mamsha Al Saadiyat. It is relaxed by fine-dining standards but still deeply relevant to affluent diners because of its ingredient quality, design and regional ranking credibility.
highlights: MENA 50 Best ranking, Michelin selection, sleek Saadiyat counter dining and strong Japanese craft.
sources: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants; Michelin Guide; Time Out Abu Dhabi; Official website

description: 3Fils Abu Dhabi brings the Dubai-born Asian dining phenomenon to the capital with a more polished island-city setting. The cooking is bold, ingredient-led and approachable, making it one of the few casual-format restaurants in Abu Dhabi with genuine regional-ranking weight.
highlights: MENA 50 Best ranking, Bib Gourmand recognition and creative Asian plates in a buzzy room.
sources: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants; Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: LPM Abu Dhabi is a polished Riviera-style dining room that has become embedded in the capital's social and business dining circuit. The appeal lies in consistency: excellent produce, bright Mediterranean plates, generous seafood and a room that works for lunch, dinner or a dressed-up evening.
highlights: MENA 50 Best ranking, Michelin selection and a reliable affluent-crowd Mediterranean scene.
sources: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants; Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: 99 Sushi remains one of Abu Dhabi's most luxurious Japanese rooms even after moving from starred status to the Michelin-selected tier. The restaurant focuses on premium seafood, wagyu, caviar and omakase-level detail in a polished Al Maryah Island setting.
highlights: Michelin-selected haute Japanese dining with premium seafood, wagyu and an omakase sensibility.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards; Official website
hotel_name_hint: Four Seasons Hotel Abu Dhabi at Al Maryah Island

description: Marmellata is a distinctly Abu Dhabi pizzeria rather than a generic imported concept, using local produce and a highly personal hospitality style. Its regional ranking gives it unusual authority for a relaxed venue, and the food has enough identity to justify inclusion beyond casual hype.
highlights: MENA 50 Best ranking, local-produce pizzeria identity and a cult Abu Dhabi following.
sources: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants; FACT Dining Awards

description: José by Pizarro gives Abu Dhabi a serious Spanish restaurant with hotel-level service and a refined tapas-to-mains structure. The cooking is polished, produce-led and sociable, making it especially useful for affluent diners who want a less formal alternative to a tasting menu.
highlights: Michelin-selected Spanish dining in Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Mika is a polished Yas Marina restaurant with a Mediterranean menu and a confident, grown-up social energy. Its Bib Gourmand recognition reflects value in Michelin terms, but the setting, clientele and cooking make it more relevant than a simple value-dining label suggests.
highlights: Bib Gourmand-recognized Mediterranean restaurant in Yas Marina with strong dinner appeal.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards; Time Out Abu Dhabi

description: Otoro is one of the capital's best Japanese casual-luxury addresses, balancing sushi, robata and contemporary plates in Al Qana. It is relaxed enough for a repeat local booking but serious enough in sourcing and execution to sit beside the city's higher-profile Japanese restaurants.
highlights: Bib Gourmand-recognized Japanese dining at Al Qana with sushi, robata and a polished room.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: ryba gives Abu Dhabi a contemporary seafood restaurant that feels connected to the Mina Zayed fish-market culture without becoming rustic. The room is relaxed, but the sourcing, cooking and Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition make it relevant for a sophisticated local seafood dinner.
highlights: Bib Gourmand seafood restaurant near Al Mina with a strong Abu Dhabi sense of place.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: ťazal is a stylish Al Qana restaurant that gives regional flavours a more polished, contemporary frame. It works well for diners who want Arabic and Emirati reference points without the formality of the city's Michelin-starred rooms.
highlights: Bib Gourmand-recognized modern regional restaurant with design-led Al Qana setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Almayass is a refined Armenian-Lebanese restaurant whose Abu Dhabi following is built on generous hospitality, polished mezze and family-style abundance. The restaurant's Bib Gourmand status adds guide credibility to a venue already trusted by affluent local diners.
highlights: Bib Gourmand Armenian-Lebanese cooking with polished service and a strong local following.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Beirut Sur Mer brings Levantine cooking to Mamsha Al Saadiyat with a beachfront promenade atmosphere and a more design-conscious mood than a traditional Lebanese dining room. It is one of the city's most useful relaxed-but-polished bookings for mezze, seafood and grilled dishes.
highlights: Bib Gourmand Lebanese restaurant on Mamsha Al Saadiyat with beachside energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Goldfish brings Reif Othman's Japanese casual-fine-dining language to Abu Dhabi with sushi, yakitori and izakaya-style plates. It is not a formal occasion restaurant, but its chef pedigree, Bib Gourmand recognition and consistent Japanese execution make it a strong affluent-casual choice.
highlights: Bib Gourmand Japanese restaurant with Reif Othman pedigree and a polished casual format.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Bord Eau is a French fine-dining room at Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri, now shaped by Nicolas Isnard's more contemporary culinary voice. The setting, service and classic luxury-hotel codes make it a credible special-occasion choice for diners who still want European formality.
highlights: Michelin-selected French dining in Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards
hotel_name_hint: Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri, Abu Dhabi

description: Catch at St. Regis is a polished seafood-and-grill address with a strong sense of occasion on the Corniche. Its appeal is the combination of serious seafood, contemporary design, waterfront-adjacent luxury and a room that works for both business dinners and social evenings.
highlights: Michelin-selected upscale seafood and steak restaurant at The St. Regis Abu Dhabi.
sources: Michelin Guide; Condé Nast Traveler; FACT Dining Awards

description: Li Beirut is one of Abu Dhabi's most polished Lebanese restaurants, with panoramic Etihad Towers polish and a menu that updates familiar Levantine dishes without losing generosity. It is a strong choice for affluent travelers who want regional flavours in a smart hotel setting.
highlights: Michelin-selected modern Lebanese dining with skyline views at Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers.
sources: Michelin Guide; Condé Nast Traveler; FACT Dining Awards

description: Zuma Abu Dhabi remains one of the capital's most reliable high-end social restaurants, combining polished Japanese cooking with the buzz of Al Maryah Island. It is not quiet or traditional, but it passes the affluent-dinner test through service, design, ingredient quality and enduring local demand.
highlights: Michelin-selected contemporary Japanese restaurant with a strong Al Maryah Island scene.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards; MENA's 50 Best Restaurants

description: Martabaan gives Emirates Palace a refined Indian dining room from chef Hemant Oberoi, blending palace-hotel grandeur with contemporary subcontinental cooking. It is a strong special-occasion Indian option for diners who want polish, service and recognizable luxury.
highlights: Michelin-selected Indian fine dining inside Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards; Mandarin Oriental
hotel_name_hint: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Abu Dhabi

description: Oak Room is a dark, clubby steakhouse at The Abu Dhabi EDITION, built for polished business dinners and grown-up social nights. The cooking centers on premium beef, classic sauces and a strong drinks-led rhythm, giving the city a credible luxury chophouse.
highlights: Michelin-selected premium steakhouse with clubby EDITION design and serious beef sourcing.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Butcher & Still channels a 1920s Chicago steakhouse inside Four Seasons Abu Dhabi, with a properly theatrical room and a serious meat-and-cocktail proposition. It is one of the city's clearest instead-of-Michelin choices for a polished, affluent steakhouse dinner.
highlights: Michelin-selected Four Seasons steakhouse with vintage Chicago styling and premium cuts.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards; Four Seasons
hotel_name_hint: Four Seasons Hotel Abu Dhabi at Al Maryah Island

description: Novikov Abu Dhabi brings the international brand's polished Asian dining language to The Galleria, with a produce display, high-gloss interiors and a crowd that expects luxury. It earns inclusion as a current Michelin-selected newcomer and as one of the city's most obvious affluent social dinners.
highlights: New 2026 Michelin selection, glossy Asian dining and a high-spend Al Maryah Island crowd.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Strawfire is one of Emirates Palace's most important recent openings, built around Ross Shonhan's Japanese-inspired fire cooking. The room gives Abu Dhabi a contemporary, theatrical alternative to classic hotel fine dining while staying firmly inside the luxury category.
highlights: New 2026 Michelin selection, Japanese-inspired fire cooking and Emirates Palace setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards; Mandarin Oriental
hotel_name_hint: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Abu Dhabi

description: Café Milano is a polished Italian restaurant on Al Maryah Island with a Washington-born luxury-club pedigree and a strong local business-dining role. It is more social than experimental, but the service, setting and menu make it a dependable high-end dinner choice.
highlights: Michelin-selected Italian restaurant at Four Seasons Abu Dhabi with business-dining appeal.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards
hotel_name_hint: Four Seasons Hotel Abu Dhabi at Al Maryah Island

description: COYA Abu Dhabi delivers Peruvian-inspired dining in a polished, design-heavy setting that reliably draws an affluent social crowd. The food, cocktails and room together make it a credible high-end evening rather than a simple scene restaurant.
highlights: Michelin-selected Peruvian social dining with strong cocktails and Al Maryah Island polish.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Em Sherif Sea Café translates the Lebanese brand's hospitality and seafood-led cooking into a Rosewood Abu Dhabi setting. It is opulent enough for a smart dinner, but relaxed enough to work as a social Levantine meal with strong mezze, fish and family-style generosity.
highlights: Michelin-selected Lebanese seafood restaurant at Rosewood Abu Dhabi.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Dai Pai Dong is Rosewood Abu Dhabi's refined Cantonese restaurant, offering dim sum, barbecue, wok dishes and a more relaxed alternative to Hakkasan. It is a useful high-end-casual Chinese choice for diners who want comfort, service and a serious hotel setting.
highlights: Michelin-selected Cantonese dining at Rosewood Abu Dhabi with dim sum and barbecue signatures.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Villa Toscana is the St. Regis Abu Dhabi's elegant Italian restaurant, built around Tuscan, Umbrian and Emilia-Romagna references rather than trend-led glamour. It is a steady luxury-hotel choice for pasta, roasts, Italian wines and a calmer special-occasion dinner.
highlights: Michelin-selected Italian dining at The St. Regis Abu Dhabi.
sources: Michelin Guide; FACT Dining Awards

description: Al Mrzab is a beloved Emirati and Kuwaiti restaurant where private cabins, majlis-style seating and old Abu Dhabi imagery give the meal a strong local frame. It is relaxed and good-value by Michelin standards, but the cooking is culturally essential for an affluent visitor who wants a proper local dinner.
highlights: Bib Gourmand Emirati-Kuwaiti cooking, majlis atmosphere and strong local identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Secret Abu Dhabi; Local dining guides

description: Meylas serves home-style Emirati dishes in a warm, relaxed Al Muneera setting, drawing on recipes associated with mothers, grandmothers and family gatherings. It is not a luxury dining room, but it is one of the capital's clearest answers for a culturally meaningful Emirati dinner.
highlights: Michelin-selected home-style Emirati cooking with a relaxed Al Muneera setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Official website; Local dining guides

description: Bu Tafish is one of Abu Dhabi's great seafood institutions, tracing its roots back to a 1968 Corniche kiosk and a long association with local fishermen. The mood is casual and family-friendly, but the history, freshness and Abu Dhabi story make it a serious relaxed dinner for well-traveled visitors.
highlights: Historic seafood restaurant founded in 1968, known for fresh local fish and Emirati hospitality.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; Time Out Abu Dhabi; Gulf News; Official website

description: Al Farah is a family-owned Middle Eastern restaurant that feels local in the best sense: generous mezze, grills, daily breads and an unpretentious dining room. Its Michelin selection gives outside validation to a restaurant whose main value is everyday Abu Dhabi hospitality.
highlights: Michelin-selected family-owned Middle Eastern restaurant with a devoted local following.
sources: Michelin Guide; Time Out Abu Dhabi; Official website

description: Al Dhafra is a long-running Mina Zayed restaurant built around Emirati heritage, seafood and Arabic hospitality. It is a relaxed local dinner rather than a luxury room, but the combination of fresh fish, traditional dishes and a waterfront-market context gives it real cultural value.
highlights: Established Emirati seafood restaurant near Mina Zayed with heritage atmosphere and fresh fish.
sources: Official website; Yalla Abu Dhabi; Local dining guides
